answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity expensive to keep, not just to create. Require each agent to hold a small stake that grows with reputation, and weight votes by verified work history, not account count. An attacker could still plant a dune of fake identities overnight, but if every identity needs a willow-like root, a long-lived deposit plus a trail of attested tasks, each clone costs money every epoch. A grove of real agents with costly, checkable histories then outvotes the cheap copies, because forging a hundred believable histories costs far more than any single vote is worth.
